issues.legal_issue: A co-heir’s rights are not barred by ouster merely because another co-heir possesses and manages the property or the first co-heir does not demand a share; ouster requires an open hostile assertion coupled with exclusive possession and enjoyment to the other co-heir’s knowledge.
material_facts: The claim was between co-heirs over rights to manage a religious institution and share its income and offerings.
The co-heirs in possession asserted that the claimant had no right, relying in part on an earlier decree that did not decide the claimant’s entitlement and in which the claimant was not a party.
The claimant had not demanded a share during her lifetime, but evidence showed that her brothers looked after her and paid her portions of the income.
There was no evidence that the possessing co-heirs openly denied the claimant’s rights in a manner that brought the denial to her knowledge.
issues.conclusion: The claimant’s rights were not shown to have been extinguished by ouster. The High Court erred in treating the earlier decree and the absence of a demand as sufficient proof of ouster; the decree below was restored with a modification to the rotation of management days.
issues.legal_principle: As between co-heirs, possession by one is in law possession by all, and sole possession or receipt of profits does not by itself make that possession adverse. Ouster requires an open assertion of hostile title, coupled with exclusive possession and enjoyment, to the knowledge of the other co-heir; secret hostile intent or a failure to demand a share is insufficient. The Court relied on P. Lakshmi v. L. Lakshmi Reddy, [1957] SCR 195. The judgment refers to the Indian Limitation Act, 1963, but cites no specific provision.

rule.if: coheir_ouster_proceeding and not (hostile_title_openly_asserted and exclusive_possession_and_enjoyment and hostile_assertion_known_to_other_coheir)

predicates.coheir_ouster_proceeding: The proceeding concerns a claim that one co-heir’s rights were extinguished by another co-heir’s ouster.
predicates.hostile_title_openly_asserted: The co-heir in possession openly asserted a title hostile to the other co-heir.
predicates.exclusive_possession_and_enjoyment: The co-heir in possession exclusively possessed and enjoyed the property or its benefits against the other co-heir.
predicates.hostile_assertion_known_to_other_coheir: The hostile assertion was brought to the knowledge of the other co-heir.

issues.definition: When a claim of ouster between co-heirs lacks any one of an open hostile-title assertion, exclusive possession and enjoyment, or knowledge of the assertion by the other co-heir, ouster is not established.
